title: A place snapshot whose source is past 30 days but whose last retry just failed is no longer reported fresh; the retry cooldown still keeps it from being run again
steps: S1: snapshotFresh / snapshotDue on a published snapshot whose google-places row was collected 35 days ago and tried one hour ago with a timeout.
S2: the same pair for a recent collection, a settled not_found answer, a never-collected setup failure and an unpublished or prefetch-only snapshot.
S3: the TripAdvisor test: a newly required source tried without data is not fresh but not due again inside its TTL.
expect: S1: snapshotFresh = false; snapshotDue = false now and true after SOURCE_RETRY_MS.
S2: fresh only for the recent collection and the settled answer within 30 days.
S3: the TripAdvisor freshness test passes.
evidence: Before the fix snapshotFresh returned !sourceDue for every source, so a 35-day-old source in its retry cooldown read fresh
fence: Data freshness (snapshotFresh) is separate from scheduling (snapshotDue / sourceDue) in places.js and joinPlace

tests: a source collected long ago whose retry just failed is stale data
a recent collection is fresh and not due
a settled "the place has nothing there" answer is fresh within the max age
a source that failed on our setup and never collected is not fresh
an unpublished or background-only snapshot is neither fresh nor spared a run
fresh snapshot is enriched for a newly enabled source
